newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: World bank to convene meeting for New Congo donors.
newsitem.headline: World bank to convene meeting for New Congo donors.

text.p: The World Bank, ending a visit to Kinshasa, said that it would hold a meeting of donors for Laurent Kabila's Congo by September and pledged support for his government.

The leader of the first Bank delegation to hold talks with the new government said the meeting would aim to mobilize resources for the recovery of the sick economy of former Zaire. "We have discussed with the government the fact that we should try to convene an informal meeting of donors that might be in a position to support this government," Callisto Madavo, vice president for the Africa region, told Reuters.
"There is a palpable determination, a very strong commitment to moving forward in this country in a different way than in the past."
Madavo, speaking before he left Congo late on Wednesday, said the meeting could be held in about eight weeks' time, or at the beginning of September.
The Bank delegation wound up its trip after meeting President Kabila, Finance Minister Mawapanga Mwana Nanga and local private investors.
Dictator Mobutu Sese Seko, who fled into exile last month, left behind a country with a foreign debt estimated at $14 billion.
Economists estimate unemployment at around 70 percent of the workforce in the nation of over 40 million people.
Kabila, who grabbed power in May after a seven-month military campaign, says road building, monetary reform and easing unemployment are priorities.
He says a new currency will be introduced but has set no date.
The World Bank closed its Kinshasa office in 1993, followed by the International Monetary Fund, when its debt payment arrears had reached 150 million dollars.
Callisto said that the Bank mission was accomplished.
"We have been able to come and re-establish contact with this new government, and to tell them that we are willing to work with them," he said.
